newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won end down on central bank dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won end down on central bank dlr buying.

text.p: The South Korean won ended weaker against the dollar on Monday on the central bank's intervention towards the close after a dull, narrow-ranged trading, dealers said.
The won closed at 888.90, down from 888.60 on Friday. It traded in a 887.80-889.30 range after opening at 888.50.
Dealers said the won was trading 887.80 won to the dollar when the Bank of Korea stepped in, buying dollars at 888.00 won. Bank of Korea officials were not available for comment.
Dealers said the won had been under upward pressure in line with the Japanese yen's recent strength against the U.S. unit.
Dealers said they estimated that the central bank bought at least $300 million on Monday.
They also said the central bank's intervention seemed to have been aimed at easing the won's tightening liquidity.
The won was seen moving sideways in a 888-890 range for the time being, but dealers did not rule out further interventions by the central bank.
The won's base mid-rate was forecast to be pegged at 888.50 on Tuesday, compared with 889.70 on Monday.
